e-4381.knowledge_point: Calculating the Value of a Scalar
e-4381.problem:
If $k {A} =
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	1 & 3 & 4 \
        	6 & 0 & -2
    	}
    	\right\rbrack,$
where ${A} =
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	2 & 6 & 8 \
        	12 & 0 & -4
    	}
    	\right\rbrack$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$
e-4381.worked_solution:
To express $kA,$ we multiply each entry of $A$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kA & =k\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 8 \\ 12 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2k & 6k & 8k \\ 12k & 0 & -4k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	2k & 6k & 8k \
        	12k & 0 & -4k
    	}
    	\right\rbrack
=
\left\lbrack
    	\matrix {
        	1 & 3 & 4 \
        	6 & 0 & -2
    	}
    	\right\rbrack
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the top-left elements, $2k$ and $1.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

e-4382.knowledge_point: Calculating a Linear Combination of Two Matrices
e-4382.worked_solution:
We multiply each entry of $A$ by $2$ and each entry of $B$ by $\dfrac{1}{2},$ and then add the resulting matrices, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2A+\frac{1}{2}B & =2[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 5 \\ 2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot 0 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 10 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2+0 & 10+1 \\ 2+2 & 4+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 11 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Dividing G by 3 gives rows (1,2,5) and (-4,3,2). Doubling H gives (2,4,10) and (6,8,12). Adding corresponding entries gives rows (3,6,15) and (2,11,14), matching option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
We multiply each entry of $G$ by $\frac{1}{3}$ and each entry of $H$ by $2,$ and then add the resulting matrices, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}G+2H & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 15 \\ -12 & 9 & 6\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}\cdot 3 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 15 \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot (-12) & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 9 & \frac{1}{3}\cdot 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 2 & 2\cdot 5 \\ 2\cdot 3 & 2\cdot 4 & 2\cdot 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 5 \\ -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 10 \\ 6 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2 & 2+4 & 5+10 \\ -4+6 & 3+8 & 2+12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 15 \\ 2 & 11 & 14\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We multiply each entry of F by 3 and each entry of G by 12, and then add the resulting matrices, as follows:

3F+12G=3[13−22]+12[2046]=[3⋅13⋅33⋅(−2)3⋅2]+[12⋅212⋅012⋅412⋅6]=[39−66]+[1023]=[3+19+0−6+26+3]=[49−49]

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Linear Combination of Two Matrices
content.worked_solution:
We multiply each entry of $F$ by $3$ and each entry of $G$ by $\frac{1}{2},$ and then add the resulting matrices, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3F+\frac{1}{2}G & =3[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\cdot 1 & 3\cdot 3 \\ 3\cdot (-2) & 3\cdot 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot 4 & \frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ -6 & 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3+1 & 9+0 \\ -6+2 & 6+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 \\ -4 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
